item.title: Koyra people fear embankment collapse
item.description:
Nearly 200,000 people in Koyra upazila of Khulna are living under the threat of flooding as erosion threatens several sections of ageing river embankments.
Severe erosion has been reported near Kobadak Station and in Mathbari, while several other sections along the Kopotakkho and Shakbaria rivers remain vulnerable to strong currents and tidal surges, residents and officials said.
The embankments protect large parts of Koyra, an area surrounded by major rivers and frequently exposed to cyclones, tidal surges and saline-water intrusion.
Residents say they face the same threat almost every year because the embankments are repeatedly repaired after breaches instead of being replaced with stronger, permanent structures.
“Just as we recover from one breach and rebuild our homes, another breach destroys everything,” said Bhabsindhu Mondal, a resident of Mathbari village.
“When saline water enters the area, trees die and mud houses collapse. We also struggle to save our cattle and other livestock,” he said.
The Water Development Board (WDB) maintains about 130km of flood-control embankments in Koyra. Most of them were built in the 1960s and have not undergone major rehabilitation, according to local officials and residents.
Cyclone Aila, which struck the region in 2009, caused extensive damage to the embankments. The damaged sections were repaired about three years later, but no comprehensive programme to construct permanent embankments followed.
Several vulnerable sections are located under Polders 13/14-1 and 13/14-2.
In July, the embankment near Kobadak Station in Golkhali of South Bedkashi Union came under severe pressure. Emergency work helped prevent a major breach, but residents fear the section could become dangerous again without a permanent solution.
Other vulnerable points have been identified in North Bedkashi and South Bedkashi, particularly along the Kopotakkho and Shakbaria rivers.
The embankment at Mathbari village in Maharajpur Union is also in critical condition, residents said.
Monirul Islam, a resident of Loka village, said repair work was taking place along the Kopotakkho River, but erosion continued to eat away at the embankment.
“Much of the area's agricultural land has already been lost to the river,” he said.
WDB officials said shrimp farming along some sections of the embankments was contributing to erosion.
According to officials, pipes are sometimes installed by cutting through embankments to move water into and out of shrimp enclosures. This weakens the structures and makes them more susceptible to erosion.
Residents, however, say stronger and more durable embankments are needed to protect communities from increasingly frequent erosion and tidal surges.
Harendranath Sarker, a member of Ward 9 of Koyra Sadar Union Parishad, said cracks had appeared near the Goriabari launch terminal along the Shakbaria River.
“If emergency measures are not taken, the embankment could disappear into the river,” he said. He also called for erosion-prevention work near a Durga temple in the area.
Former Koyra Upazila Parishad vice-chairman Advocate A Rashid said many embankments had become too low to withstand tidal surges.
“Water now overflows into settlements during high tides because the embankments have not been raised or reinforced for a long time,” he said.
He identified embankments at Dashhalia, Gilabari, No. 4 Koyra, Mathbari, Katkata, Sardarghat and Tetultala as particularly vulnerable.
Mashiul Abedin, section officer of the WDB's Amadi section in Koyra, said some vulnerable sections had already been repaired and were now considered relatively safe.
“Koyra is surrounded by several major rivers, and some sections of the embankments remain vulnerable. We have informed the higher authorities about those areas,” he said.
Shahnewaz, executive engineer of the WDB's Satkhira Zone, said repair work was underway at some vulnerable points.
“Contractors have been appointed to repair the remaining vulnerable sections, and work is ongoing,” he said.
“If an emergency arises, immediate measures will be taken through the contractors,” he added.

item.title: Rain brings relief to Aman farmers in Rajshahi
item.description:
Recent rainfall has revived Aman paddy fields across Rajshahi, easing farmers’ concerns over prolonged dry weather and rising irrigation costs during the crop’s crucial flowering and grain-filling stages.
The Rajshahi Meteorological Office recorded 99.4 millimetres of rain, the highest this season, after several days of dry weather. The rainfall has restored moisture in the fields and reduced farmers’ dependence on irrigation, raising hopes of a better harvest.
“The rain has not caused any damage to my paddy fields. Rather, it has been a great benefit,” said Nazir Uddin, a farmer in Ujirpur, Paba upazila, who has cultivated Aman on five and a half bighas.
“The plants have become fresh and healthy after receiving rainwater,” he said.
Nazir Uddin harvested about 22 maunds of paddy per bigha last year and expects a good yield again this season.
Farmers say irrigation from BMDA deep tube wells costs about Tk 250 per bigha per round. The recent rain could eliminate the need for two to three rounds of irrigation, saving as much as Tk 1,000 per bigha, they said.
Rainwater also helps wash dust from paddy leaves and may reduce heat-related stress and the risk of some pests and diseases, farmers said.
“Rainwater is a blessing for Aman paddy. It reduces expenses on both irrigation and pesticides,” said Astan Ali, a farmer from Kharkhari in Paba. He harvested about 20 maunds per bigha last year and is hoping for a good yield this year.
According to the Department of Agricultural Extension, Aman paddy has been cultivated on 82,452 hectares in Rajshahi this season, with a production target of 314,336 metric tonnes.
Farmers have been busy preparing seedbeds, transplanting seedlings, applying fertiliser and tending their crops. But the prolonged dry spell had increased their reliance on irrigation and raised production costs.
Agricultural officials said the timing of the rainfall was particularly favourable because Aman plants are now at the flowering and grain-filling stages, when adequate moisture is essential for healthy development and yield.
Mostafa Kamal Hossain, deputy director of the Rajshahi Department of Agricultural Extension, said the district had achieved broad coverage of modern varieties and farming technologies this season.
“If weather conditions remain favourable, we expect the district to achieve its production target,” he said.

item.title: Teacher’s death in snatching: Three accused sent to jail
item.description:
Three accused in the case over the death of primary school headteacher Ranjila Parveen have been sent to jail after completing five days of remand.
Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Md Ripon Hossain passed the order on Saturday following a petition from the investigation officer. Prosecution Department Sub-Inspector Rafiqul Islam confirmed the matter.
The accused are Poni, alias Para Poni and Poni Gazi; Cedric Julian; and Rakib Hossain.
Sher-e-Bangla Nagar police Sub-Inspector Shahin, also the case investigation officer, produced the three before the court after their remand and sought their detention in jail.
No bail petition was filed on their behalf, and the court subsequently ordered them sent to jail.
Earlier on Monday, the court granted the three five days of remand. Before that, Rapid Action Battalion (RAB)-2 arrested them during a drive and seized a Yamaha R15 motorcycle allegedly used in the snatching.
According to the case documents, Ranjila Parveen, 56, was the headteacher of Bagbari Government Primary School in Bogra’s Gabtali upazila.
On August 29, she was traveling to Dhaka with her husband, Md Abdul Matin, to visit an ophthalmologist.
At around 5:55am, when they reached the road near Gate 12 of the National Parliament Building on Manik Mia Avenue, motorcycle-riding snatchers allegedly pulled her handbag.
Ranjila fell from the moving autorickshaw onto the road and suffered a serious head injury.
She was rescued and taken to Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital in critical condition. She was later declared dead while being taken to Dhaka Medical College Hospital.
Following the incident, her husband filed a case with Sher-e-Bangla Nagar police station.

item.title: PM: Some political parties trying to create anarchy by exploiting crises
item.description:
Prime Minister and BNP Chairman Tarique Rahman on Saturday accused some political parties and individuals of trying to create anarchy by exploiting the country’s ongoing power and gas crises inherited by his administration, saying everyone should act within their limits.
“We are trying to resolve all the problems we have inherited, whether from the authoritarian regime or the interim government,” he said while speaking at a discussion meeting marking the BNP’s 48th founding anniversary.
Tarique Rahman acknowledged that there are problems in various sectors that are causing suffering to the people.
“But we are noticing that some political parties and individuals are trying in different ways to create confusion by exploiting these problems, and through this confusion they are trying to create anarchy in the country,” he said.
The prime minister said the government will uphold the democratic process and make its utmost effort to maintain democratic principles and ethics.
“But if anyone wants to create anarchy, the law of the country clearly sets out how to control such anarchy. Therefore, as a government—and not just as a government, but as a government elected by the people—I want to make it clear that everyone needs to remain within their respective limits,” he said.
The discussion was held at the auditorium of the Krishibid Institution Bangladesh (KIB) in Farmgate.
At the beginning of the program, participants observed a one-minute silence in memory of BNP founder Ziaur Rahman, former BNP Chairperson Khaleda Zia and all those who sacrificed their lives for the country and the party.
The event began with the national anthem, followed by the party anthem and a documentary on the BNP.
President Ziaur Rahman founded the BNP on September 1, 1978. The five-day central program marking the party’s 48th founding anniversary, which began on Tuesday, concluded with Saturday’s discussion.
Tarique Rahman said the BNP inherited a fragile economy, as well as weak health, education and communication systems, after forming the government.
He identified the energy crisis as the country’s biggest immediate problem, acknowledging that many people and industries are suffering from shortages of electricity and fuel.
“I apologize on behalf of the party to all those who are suffering from the shortage of electricity and fuel,” the BNP chief said.
He, however, said the government did not want to use the problems left behind by the previous regime or the interim government merely as excuses.
“We do not want to simply cite these problems as excuses. Rather, we want to present the reality to the people and at the same time take measures so that people do not have to face such problems in the future,” the prime minister said.
He said the BNP has already adopted an action plan to address the energy crisis and prepare the country to withstand possible future global disruptions.
“An action plan requires time to formulate, and implementing it also requires some time,” Tarique Rahman said, adding that the government is taking its measures keeping possible future global crises in mind.
He alleged that a political group operated in disguise during the previous authoritarian regime and that some of its members subsequently admitted their involvement.
The prime minister also accused some political parties of attempting to spread confusion and said such activities could create an opportunity for forces associated with the ousted authoritarian regime to return to the political scene.
“Could it be that those who remained hidden under the authoritarian regime are now, from within that hidden network, trying to incite this anarchy?” he asked.
“If that is the case, then those who are hiding are actually working to bring that authoritarian regime back to the forefront,” Tarique Rahman said.
Calling on all nationalist forces and BNP leaders and activists, he said: “Let us make the people more aware. Let us expose to the people who is taking responsibility for whom and who is trying to protect whom.”
The prime minister alleged that certain political forces had protected or sheltered one another at different points in Bangladesh’s history.
“This politics must be exposed before the people. We have to make it clear to the people. Because we have seen these forces, operating covertly, shielding and sheltering one another at different times over the years and decades—whether in 1971, 1986, 1996, over the past one and a half decades, or even today," he said.
“So today, we have to expose their politics before the people. We have to make it clear to the people," Tarique Rahman said.
He said the BNP had consistently sought to establish a democratic system and uphold the democratic rights of the people since the party’s inception.
“We still firmly believe in this,” the prime minister said, adding that hundreds of thousands of BNP leaders and activists had sacrificed their lives for democracy.
At the same time, he said, the BNP wants to build a humane state and a democracy where no one would face obstacles in exercising their rights.

item.title: Indian police file FIR against politician over offering namaz
item.description:
Indian police have filed a first information report (FIR) against a Samajwadi Party politician for offering namaz on a road at a government circuit house in Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh.
The FIR was filed against Samajwadi Party district vice-president Haji Mohammad Usman under Sections 285 and 292 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, which deal with obstruction of a public way and public nuisance, reports The Wire.
Usman was seen offering prayers behind a parked car in a video that has circulated widely on social media. He is the uncle of Bilari MLA Mohammad Faheem Irfan.
Usman had visited the circuit house to attend a meeting between Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council Leader of the Opposition Lal Bihari Yadav and Samajwadi Party leaders.
The FIR followed a complaint by Anit Kumar, an assistant engineer in charge of the provincial division of the Public Works Department in Moradabad.
Kumar alleged in his complaint that Usman had parked his vehicle on a route used for entering and exiting the Circuit House and offered prayers behind the vehicle, obstructing the movement of vehicles and people.
The video cited in the report, however, does not appear to show anyone being obstructed by the prayers. The people and vehicles visible in the footage are not seen moving through the area at the time.
The incident has drawn criticism from local Hindutva groups. Dainik Bhaskar reported that members of such groups questioned how prayers were allowed at the government premises.
Offering prayers at government premises is not in itself illegal, although the Uttar Pradesh government has criminalized offering namaz on roads.
The police action against Usman has also prompted comparisons with the Kanwar Yatra, during which participants have been accused in widely circulated videos of blocking roads, vandalizing vehicles and establishments, and making vulgar gestures.
The FIR provisions cited against Usman carry penalties related to public obstruction and nuisance, although the circumstances surrounding the alleged obstruction remain disputed.

item.title: Two Nepal rescues revive hopes 10 days after flood
item.description:
Rescuers in Nepal pulled alive on Saturday a Chinese national from a tunnel and a local woman from her partially submerged home, as emergency response teams searched with renewed vigour for thousands missing since catastrophic flooding 10 days ago.
A rescue team comprising personnel from the Nepal Army and foreign experts rescued the Chinese man from 225 meters (738 feet) inside the tunnel of the Upper Trishuli-1 Hydropower Project in Rasuwa district, a military statement said.
A picture of the rescue published on the army’s Facebook page showed the man, identified only as Luhaitao, with his arms around the shoulders of two camouflage-clad rescuers.
He appeared alert, but his hands were covered in thick, wet mud.
“His health is currently being assessed and further search and rescue operations are continuing,” the army said.
The man was among hundreds of hydropower workers who went missing after a tsunami-like wall of water and mud swept through the China-Nepal border following a vast glacial and rock collapse on August 26.
Authorities later in the day said members of Nepal’s Armed Police Force pulled alive Chandrika Shrestha, 64, from her buried home in Nuwakot district.
“A police team found her as they were clearing the area. She has been airlifted to Kathmandu for treatment,” police deputy superintendent Iqbal Hawari told AFP.
A video released by Nepal’s Armed Police Force showed only part of her house visible, with the lower floors submerged by thick sludge.
On Friday, two Nepali hydropower workers were rescued at the Trishuli 3A tunnel, where searches continued alongside multiple other sites, with at least 12 hydropower projects destroyed by the floods.
Both men were reported to be in stable condition in a Kathmandu hospital.
So far, 1,344 bodies have been recovered in Nepal, according to the national disaster agency, with around 5,000 people missing.
In China, state media said 31 people had been killed and 531 were missing.
That takes the overall death toll to 1,375 people, and more than 5,500 missing.
The government initially said it believed more than 100 workers could be alive inside multiple tunnels.
Experts from India, China, Australia and South Korea have been aiding Nepali rescuers in their search of survivors inside the blocked tunnels.
Rescuers have also been relying on drones to deliver medicine, food and other supplies, as well as transporting bodies, in high-altitude areas hard to reach by roads.
“We have sent a lot of relief material and right now our team is loading some materials for the hospital in the area,” drone operator Avaya Pokharel told AFP in Nuwakot.
The United Nations has warned that the “magnitude of the destruction” makes delivering aid an immense challenge, launching a $50 million appeal to help more than 84,000 people affected by the disaster.
With morgues overflowing, some 1,030 bodies have been buried in mass graves after taking DNA samples for future identification, Nepal Police said on Saturday.
Prime Minister Balendra Shah promised to provide “safe and comfortable accommodation” for thousands of people displaced by the disaster and currently living in temporary relief camps.
“We know that staying there (in camps) is not easy for you,” he said in a social media post on Friday.
He promised to “once again create an environment where you can dream about and build your future.”

item.title: PM: People have relied on BNP during every crisis
item.description:
Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) Chairman and Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has said people have always relied on the BNP during times of crisis, with the party addressing various challenges in the past by working with its leaders and activists.
“Currently, the country's biggest problem is the fuel crisis. We are not denying it. But the crisis has been created by global factors,” he said while speaking as the chief guest at a discussion organized to mark the BNP's 48th founding anniversary at the Krishibid Institution in Khamarbari, Dhaka, on Saturday afternoon.
Tarique said the government was working on a master plan to ensure the country does not face similar problems in the future.
Acting secretary general Ruhul Kabir Rizvi chaired the meeting, which was also addressed by central party leaders.
Tarique said people's democratic rights had been taken away in the past and the country's economic foundation had been weakened.
“Therefore, as in the past, in the previous election too, people voted for the BNP in a majority of seats and gave it the opportunity to form the government,” he said.
Tarique said the government inherited a fragile economy after coming to power.
He said the war had created a fuel and power crisis, but expressed hope that the situation would be resolved soon.

item.title: Expressway body identified as missing Gazipur man
item.description:
The body found on the Dhaka Elevated Expressway has been identified as that of Ismail Hossain, 50, a resident of Gazipur.
Ismail went missing while returning to Gazipur from his village in Jamalpur with Tk5 lakh from the sale of land for his daughter’s wedding.
Banani police OC Faridul Islam told Dhaka Tribune that police had identified the car used to dump Ismail’s body and expected to arrest those involved soon.
“This will help us determine who was involved in the incident. We hope it will be possible to arrest them soon,” he said.
Ismail’s relatives identified the body at Dhaka Medical College Hospital on Saturday after police informed them. The body was later handed over to the family following an autopsy.
Ismail was the son of Jalal Uddin of Jamalpur Sadar upazila.
Relatives said Ismail’s only daughter, Sharmin, was set to get married. He had sold 11 decimals of land in the village for Tk10.5 lakh to arrange money for the wedding and was returning to Gazipur to finalize the wedding date.
However, he went missing on the way.
His son Hasan said Ismail had Tk5 lakh and two mobile phones with him when he left Jamalpur, but neither the money nor the phones was found.
“My father left Jamalpur for Gazipur at around 3:30am on Thursday. At around 11pm, he called me and said he would arrive in the morning,” Hasan said.
“He was returning to Gazipur to finalize discussions about my younger sister Sharmin’s wedding. He was supposed to set the wedding date after coming home.”
Hasan said his father had repaid a Tk2 lakh loan with part of the money from the land sale and used some of the remaining money to build a room at their village home.
“He was returning to Gazipur with the remaining Tk5 lakh in cash and some groceries. He also had an Android phone and a button phone with him. Neither was found,” he said.
Hasan said his father was supposed to get off at Jirani in Gazipur on Friday morning. He went there and called him several times, but Ismail’s phone was switched off.
Later, Banani police informed Jamalpur police about the matter. Hasan then went to DMCH and identified his father’s body.
Police recovered Ismail’s body from the Dhaka Elevated Expressway on Friday. His mouth had been taped shut, and he was wearing a blue shirt and lungi similar to those worn by auto-rickshaw drivers.
Banani police SI Nazrul Islam Talukdar said Ismail’s identity was confirmed by matching his fingerprints with the National Identity Card database.
Quoting relatives, he said Ismail had worked as a security guard at Delta Spinning Mill but left the job about nine months ago due to illness.
He lived in Kashimpur, Gazipur, with his wife, two children and daughter-in-law. About four months ago, he had gone to his village home in Jamalpur, where his mother and elder sister live.
Police suspect Ismail was strangled to death before his body was brought to the expressway and dumped there.
“We suspect that he was strangled to death and his body was brought in a car and dumped,” SI Nazrul Islam said.
He said police were collecting CCTV footage as part of the investigation. A case has been filed by the deceased’s family.

item.title: Zahid: Recognition of everyone’s role essential to build inclusive society
item.description:
Women and Children Affairs and Social Welfare Minister Abu Zafar Md. Zahid Hossain on Saturday said that recognizing everyone’s contributions to the society can make it easier to resolve many social problems.
“If we can sincerely embrace and use the word ‘we’ instead of ‘I’ in the society, then it will become more beautiful and inclusive,” he said while addressing the 10th biennial conference of the Bangladesh Institute of Labour Studies (BILS) at the Institution of Diploma Engineers, Bangladesh (IDEB) auditorium as the chief guest.
The minister said Prime Minister Tarique Rahman is working relentlessly to build an inclusive Bangladesh where people from all sections of the society and all professions are being given the highest priority. “Every person living in the society is a worker in one way or another. The only difference is in the nature and field of their work,” he said.
He said the government is implementing a nationwide Family Card distribution programme as part of its commitment to ensure social security and welfare for marginalized workers as well as disadvantaged and destitute people.
Speaking as a special guest, Prime Minister’s Adviser Mahdi Amin said fair wages are neither an act of charity nor merely a matter of demand; rather, it’s a legitimate right and entitlement of workers. He said the government, elected with the spontaneous trust of 75 million working people, is committed to ensuring their overall welfare.
Emphasizing the importance of sustainable industries and a fair working environment, Mahdi Amin stressed the need for mutual trust among the workers, employers and the government, along with regular tripartite dialogue.
Speakers at the conference called for necessary reforms to labour laws for ensuring legal recognition, institutional registration and social protection for all workers. They also demanded the determination of fair wages that would enable workers to live with dignity and support their personal development.

item.title: Dulu: All involved in Rangpur four murders to face justice
item.description:
Disaster Management and Relief Minister Asadul Habib Dulu on Saturday said all involved in the killing of schoolteacher Ganapati Chakraborty and three members of his family in Rangpur will be identified and brought to justice.
“Everyone involved, including those behind the scenes, will be identified and brought under the law. The trial will be completed as quickly as possible,” he told journalists after laying the foundation stone for a six-storey building for the Burn and Plastic Surgery Unit at Rangpur Medical College Hospital.
Calling the killings “horrific and tragic,” Dulu said such a brutal incident had never occurred in Rangpur before. He said several theories had emerged surrounding the murders, making the investigation complex.
“We want to identify everyone involved. That is why the investigation is taking time. A crime of this magnitude cannot be uncovered within such a short period. However, we are working to identify the killers, masterminds and others involved and ensure a speedy trial,” he said.
Dulu assured that no innocent person would be implicated and only the actual perpetrators would face justice.
Regarding Rangpur Medical College Hospital, he said the government was working to resolve its longstanding problems and would ensure adequate ICU beds within a month. He alleged that corruption and misappropriation hindered development over the past 17 years.
Hospital director Brigadier General Ashikur Rahman and senior officials were present.

item.title: Thakurgaon ready to welcome President on first hometown visit
item.description:
Thakurgaon is buzzing with preparations to welcome Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir on his first visit to his hometown as President.
Alleys, markets, neighborhoods and roads once familiar to him are now being ready for his arrival with an atmosphere of festivity prevailing. Arches are being erected at various points and decorative lights installed, while administrative officials and employees, political leaders and activists are working round the clock. Municipal workers are also working day and night to make the town clean and orderly.
People are eagerly awaiting the President’s arrival, with growing curiosity and excitement among ordinary residents alongside the extensive administrative preparations.
President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir is scheduled to arrive in his home district on a two-day official visit Sunday.
The district administration has made extensive preparations for the state visit, public interest and emotion surrounding it appeared even greater.
Security measures have also been strengthened across the district. Members of the Special Security Force (SSF), President Guard Regiment (PGR) and intelligence agencies are working at the field level, while additional security has been put in place at the scheduled venues, along travel routes and in other important areas.
Convener of the President’s Reception Committee Dr Abu Md Khairul Kabir said, “He is not only the President, he is a son of Thakurgaon. After a long time, he is returning to his own people while holding the country’s highest constitutional post.” “His return is a moment of immense pride and emotion for us. We want the people of Thakurgaon to welcome him with love and respect,” he added.
District BNP President Mirza Faisal Amin said the President’s first visit to his home district is a matter of joy, pride and emotion for the people of Thakurgaon. He said the President has a longstanding emotional bond with the people of the district, and his visit has generated widespread enthusiasm and excitement among people from all walks of life.

Saif Sarwar receives 2nd IMFA nomination
item.description:
Bangladeshi automotive filmmaker and content creator Saif Sarwar has received his 2nd consecutive nomination at the International Motor Film Awards (IMFA) for his film “Beyond The Machine”.
Sarwar became the first Bangladeshi filmmaker to receive an IMFA nomination in 2025 for “Go Beyond”. His latest nomination makes him a 2-time consecutive nominee.
Featuring the Porsche 718 Boxster, “Beyond The Machine” explores the creative vision behind automotive filmmaking and the work involved in shaping how a vehicle is presented on screen.
The IMFA 2026 nominations also include productions such as “Crime 101”, “The Running Man”, “TRON: Ares” and “The Rip”, alongside other films and automotive productions featuring internationally known actors and creators.
The 2026 IMFA Awards Night is scheduled for November 14 at the Petersen Automotive Museum in Los Angeles, California.
For Sarwar, attending the ceremony is now a bigger challenge than securing another nomination. He was invited to the 2025 awards night in London but could not attend because he was unable to secure financial support.
“Being nominated at IMFA for the second time makes me feel more afraid than happy,” Sarwar said. “I know how difficult it is to reach this stage, but for an automotive filmmaker from Bangladesh, turning that dream into reality is even harder.”
“I make automotive films simply because I love doing it. But in Bangladesh, automotive filmmaking still does not receive the recognition or value it deserves,” he said.
Sarwar has received a direct invitation to this year’s ceremony in Los Angeles.
“This year, the awards are taking place in Los Angeles, Hollywood. I have even received a direct invitation letter from the awards director, but my biggest fear is still the same, will I once again miss the chance to stand there and receive my certificate with my own hands?” he said.
“As a Bangladeshi creator, perhaps my biggest challenge is not getting nominated, it is actually getting there. I want to see with my own eyes the dream I started with my country’s name attached to it finally reach its destination,” he said.
In 2025, Sarwar also became the first Bangladeshi creator to receive a “Judges Honorable Mention” at the Grand Motoring Film Festival in the United States.

item.title: Shafiqur: On streets until people’s demands are met
item.description:
Leader of the Opposition and Jamaat-e-Islami Ameer Dr Shafiqur Rahman on Saturday said they would remain on the streets until the people’s demands are fulfilled, accusing the government of deceiving people and breaking its promises.
“We have taken to the streets to realise the people’s demands. We will return home only after those demands are fulfilled,” he said while addressing a rally at Paduar Bazar Biswaroad in Comilla as part of Dhaka-Chittagong long march led by the Jamaat-led 11-party alliance.
He said people shed blood on the streets in the struggle against authoritarianism but their demands have not yet been fulfilled.
The Jamaat chief said the alliance has taken to the streets to press for implementation of the public mandate in the referendum and the spirit of the July mass uprising. “We have come to the streets to restore gas supplies to your homes and ensure electricity.”
He also questioned whether people are receiving uninterrupted electricity and gas and whether extortion is taking place. He said the country is overwhelmed by drugs and called for effective measures to control the problem.
Jamaat Naib-e-Ameer and Deputy Leader of the Opposition Dr Abdullah Muhammad Taher also addressed the rally, calling for implementation of the alliance’s six-point demand and the referendum mandate.
National Citizen Party (NCP) Convener and Opposition Chief Whip Nahid Islam said uninterrupted supplies of oil, gas and electricity must be ensured. He warned that the government would not be able to remain in office if it fails to meet the people’s basic demands.
Liberal Democratic Party Chairman Colonel (retd) Oli Ahmed said the mandate given by 70 percent of people must be implemented, warning that the government would have to be made to fail if the mandate was not automatically implemented.
Bangladesh Khelafat Majlis Ameer Mamunul Haque said people must remain prepared to face tougher challenges ahead to change their fortunes and take the country in the right direction.
He said the long march marked the beginning of the second phase of the ongoing movement. The Dhaka-Chittagong long march began in the capital on Saturday morning with the alliance’s six-point demands.
After holding roadside rallies at different locations, including Shimrail in Narayanganj, the procession reached Cumilla and held the rally at Paduar Bazar Bishwaroad before heading towards Chattogram.
Leaders of the 11-party alliance and local Jamaat leaders also attended the programme.
Their six-point demands are the implementation of people's verdict in the February 12 referendum, trial of the July 2024 mass killings, resolution of the multi-dimensional energy crisis, measures to control soaring prices of essential commodities, an end to extortion and corruption and improvement of the law and order situation and an end to narrow partisanisation.

item.title: One detained after alleged snatching at Mugda hospital
item.description:
A man was detained while allegedly attempting to flee after snatching a mobile phone and a bag at Mugda Medical College Hospital in the capital.
The detained man was identified as Nazmul Alam Biplob.
Md Najmus Sakib, deputy director (public relations) of Bangladesh Ansar, said on Saturday morning that the incident took place around noon on Friday in front of ICU-1 on the hospital’s sixth floor.
Taking advantage of the crowd of critically ill patients and their relatives, Biplob allegedly attempted to flee with the mobile phone and bag.
An Ansar team led by member Md Zakiul Islam, who was on duty at the hospital, caught him in the act, Sakib said.
A search of the suspect led to the recovery of the stolen mobile phone and bag intact, he added.
The matter was subsequently reported to the hospital authorities. Following their instructions, Biplob was handed over to police at the local police station.

item.title: 11-party opposition alliance launches Dhaka-Chittagong march
item.description:
The 11-party opposition alliance led by Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami launched a Dhaka-Chittagong long march yesterday, warning that its street movement would intensify unless the government addresses its demands.
The alliance is demanding implementation of the referendum verdict, justice for the July killings, and measures to ease shortages of electricity, gas, fuel and fertilizer, control rising prices, improve law and order and end what it describes as narrow, partisan politics.
Jamaat-e-Islami Ameer and Leader of the Opposition Dr Shafiqur Rahman said the alliance had taken to the streets for people’s rights and would continue its movement until those rights were ensured.
“Our long march is for the people of 180 million. We have taken to the streets for their rights and will return home only after securing those rights,” he said at the opening rally at Shapla Chattar in Motijheel.
The march began around 8:30am and was scheduled to culminate in a rally at Laldighi Maidan in Chittagong in the evening.
Speaking at a roadside rally in Mahipal, Feni, around 4pm, Shafiqur warned that the alliance was prepared to escalate the movement.
“We are giving this government some time, but this time will not be long. Stay prepared. When the final call comes, you and all of us will have to come out onto the streets, putting our lives at stake,” he said.
He said the movement would continue both on the streets and inside parliament until people’s rights were ensured.
“We know everyone. We know who has how much courage,” Shafiqur said, adding that it would not take 17 years to drive out anyone seeking to establish “new fascism” in Bangladesh.
At the Feni rally, he accused the government of failing to address shortages of electricity, gas and water and rising prices.
“Actually, the people of the country are not well. They really are not well. Is there electricity at this moment? No,” he said.
He alleged that electricity was available inside parliament and at the residences of the power minister while ordinary people were suffering from shortages.
Shafiqur said people wanted uninterrupted electricity, gas and water, as well as essential goods at affordable prices.
He also called for justice for the Shapla massacre, the killings of 57 army officers at Pilkhana, the killings carried out across the country over 15 years and the July killings.
“We have both said that if the referendum wins, if the ‘Yes’ wins, we will accept it and fully implement it. Has the current government implemented it? No,” he said, accusing the government of failing to honor its commitment to implement the referendum verdict.
Shafiqur said the alliance had taken to the streets not for any particular party or to make anyone a leader, but because it was hearing “the footsteps of fascism” again.
“The responsibility of the brave is that wherever the rights of the people are pulled away, they will roar there, resist there, protest there and build a protest there,” he said.
He also called for the release of a young man named Sifat, who was reportedly arrested after making comments expressing frustration over public suffering.
“Release him peacefully. If you do not, remember that incidents involving Nur Hossain, Yasmin and Dr Milon once changed the course of politics,” he said.
Opposition Chief Whip Nahid Islam said the long march represented the people and warned that the movement could intensify if the government tried to obstruct it.
“If the government creates obstacles to the long march, the six demands of the 11-party alliance will turn into one demand,” he said.
Jamaat Secretary General Mia Golam Parwar accused the government of failing to reduce public suffering and breaking its promises on implementation of the referendum verdict.
“The government must admit its mistakes in parliament and take steps to reform the Constitution to implement the July Charter,” he said.
Liberal Democratic Party President Col (retd) Oli Ahmed also warned the government to respond to the people’s demands.
“If the demands of the people are not accepted, we will be forced to make the government accept them,” he said.
Bangladesh Khilafat Majlis Ameer Maulana Mamunul Haque said the government would face consequences if it failed to understand the message of the long march.
NCP President Nahid Islam accused the BNP of establishing “parliamentary autocracy” and alleged that corruption and syndicates had contributed to the country’s fuel crisis.
“If the referendum verdict is not implemented and the ongoing crises involving the country’s oil and gas are not resolved, you will not be able to remain in power,” he said at the Feni rally.
The roadside rally was chaired by Feni district Jamaat Ameer Mufti Abdul Hannan. AB Party’s Mujibur Rahman Manju and other central leaders of the 11 parties also spoke.
After the opening rally in Dhaka, the procession moved toward Chittagong along the Dhaka-Chittagong Highway.
The alliance planned roadside rallies at the truck stand area near Chittagong Road in Narayanganj, Paduar Bazar in Comilla, Chauddagram, Mahipal in Feni and Mirsharai in Chittagong before the final rally at Laldighi Maidan around 7pm.
The schedule could change depending on the situation, alliance leaders said.
The alliance had earlier said vehicles participating in the march would use one side of the highway, allowing regular traffic to continue on the other.
Leaders also held meetings with police officials to keep the program peaceful and organized and apologized in advance for possible public inconvenience caused by the march.
The Chittagong-bound march is the first in a planned series. The alliance plans similar programs toward Rangpur on September 19, Khulna on October 31 and Sylhet on November 21, followed by a larger program in Dhaka.

Dengue surge prompts stronger measures in Khulna, Chittagong, Barisal
item.description:
Dengue cases are rising rapidly in Khulna, Chittagong and Barisal, prompting the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) to strengthen prevention measures and prepare hospitals for a possible surge in patients.
The health authorities have instructed city corporations, civil surgeon offices and hospitals to step up control efforts, arrange additional beds, open dengue corners, spray insecticides regularly in high-risk areas and conduct mobile courts.
According to DGHS data, 988 dengue patients were admitted to hospitals across the country in the past 24 hours, while two died during the same period.
The latest figures have taken the year's total cases to 41,032 and the death toll to 113.
Khulna Division has recorded the highest number of cases, with 6,487 patients admitted and 19 deaths so far. Barisal has reported 6,379 cases and Chittagong 6,178.
Dhaka Division has recorded 6,017 cases, followed by Dhaka South City Corporation with 5,400, Dhaka North City Corporation with 4,895, Mymensingh with 2,267, Rajshahi with 2,230, Rangpur with 1,005 and Sylhet with 184.
Constant monitoring
Professor Dr Nurul Islam, director of the hospital division at DGHS, told Dhaka Tribune that the authorities are maintaining constant monitoring to tackle dengue and other seasonal diseases.
“Cases are comparatively increasing in Khulna, Barisal and Chittagong. So, directions are being given to the concerned city corporations and civil surgeons every day through Zoom meetings,” he said.
Authorities are also reviewing prevention activities regularly to ensure they are being implemented properly, he said.
Mobile courts have been ordered in areas with a high prevalence of Aedes mosquito larvae, while regular insecticide spraying has been ordered in the morning and afternoon.
Civil surgeon offices have also been instructed to coordinate their efforts with city corporations.
Dr Nurul said authorities at a meeting last week with all civil surgeons and directors and superintendents of government hospitals were instructed to arrange additional beds and ensure necessary treatment preparations if patient pressure increases.
Professor Dr Foyara Tasnim, additional director general (Planning and Development) of DGHS, said dengue testing facilities have been ensured at all government hospitals.
The maximum testing fee has also been fixed for private hospitals to protect patients from additional costs, she said.
Dengue corners have been ordered at government and private hospitals, while regular coordination meetings with divisional directors and civil surgeons are being held to monitor the situation.
As cases increase outside Dhaka, hospitals have been instructed to keep additional beds ready, she said.
The national guideline for dengue patient admission, testing and treatment has also been distributed among relevant institutions. Sufficient stocks of saline, diagnostic kits and other treatment equipment are available, she added.
Jahangirnagar University entomologist Professor Dr Kabirul Bashar said Aedes mosquitoes are present in almost all cities across the country, creating conditions for dengue transmission.
However, he said mosquito density alone does not mean infections will begin simultaneously in all areas.
“When a dengue-infected person enters an area, local Aedes mosquitoes can acquire the virus from the person and later transmit it to others. This is how the disease can spread rapidly within a short period,” he said.
Insecticide spraying alone cannot control Aedes mosquitoes because many breeding sites are difficult to reach, Bashar said.
He recommended using insect growth regulator (IGR) tablets at permanent breeding sites, such as water meter holes, which can suppress mosquito reproduction for several months.
Khulna City Corporation Conservancy Officer Md Wahiduzzaman said an additional 155 spraymen have been deployed across 31 wards alongside regular larvicide and adulticide operations.
Morning and afternoon fogging is being conducted at designated dengue hospitals to prevent mosquitoes from spreading from hospital areas.
Cleaning of bushes, drains and canals, removing waterlogging and regular spraying are also continuing, including on holidays.
“We are carrying out morning and afternoon fogging in areas where mosquito larvae are likely to be found. Mobile courts are also continuing,” he said.
Khulna Deputy Civil Surgeon Dr Md Shawkat Ali said medical teams have been formed in coordination with the city corporation.
Awareness campaigns are being conducted in areas with high infection rates, while upazila-level activities are also being monitored regularly.
A rally will soon be organized under the leadership of the district administration, he said.
Barisal City Corporation Conservancy Officer Muhammad Yusuf Ali said regular mobile courts, drain and canal cleaning, and joint drives with the health department are underway.
The activities are being carried out in line with instructions issued at a recent Secretariat meeting, he said.
The Ministry of Local Government has also ordered stronger preventive measures following the deaths of four people in a single day.
Yusuf said the number of cases may appear higher in institutional statistics because patients are often transferred from village hospitals to upazila, district and divisional hospitals, resulting in the same patient being counted by multiple institutions.
A high number of Aedes larvae have also been found in water accumulated in coconut and areca nut tree trunks in parts of Pirojpur. Special spraying is being conducted there.
In Chittagong, eight of the city's 41 wards have been identified as dengue hotspots through a joint survey by the city corporation, civil surgeon's office and health department, said Mosquito Control Officer Sarful Islam Mahi.
A 60-member special team has been formed and trained to work in the hotspots.
Another 192 areas have been identified as red zones, where morning and afternoon spraying, mobile courts and awareness campaigns through loudspeakers are being conducted.
Insecticide is also being applied within a 500-metre radius of the homes of dengue patients, he said.
“We are leaving no stone unturned in taking the necessary measures to prevent dengue,” Mahi said.

item.title: Body dumped on expressway: Vehicle driver arrested
item.description:
Rapid Action Battalion-1 (RAB-1) has arrested the driver of a vehicle allegedly used to dump the body of a man on the Dhaka Elevated Expressway.
The arrestee was identified as Sohel Rana, 40. RAB-1 said he was arrested in the capital’s Mohakhali area on Saturday.
Police had earlier identified the vehicle used to dump the body of Ismail Hossain, 50, and said they were working to identify those involved in the incident.
Ismail’s body was recovered from the Dhaka Elevated Expressway by Banani police on Friday. His mouth was wrapped in scotch tape, and he was wearing a blue shirt and lungi similar to clothing commonly worn by autorickshaw drivers.
Police suspect Ismail was strangled to death before his body was transported and dumped on the expressway.
Ismail, a resident of Kashimpur in Gazipur, had been returning from his village home in Jamalpur with money from the sale of land for his daughter’s wedding.
After being informed by police, relatives went to Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH) on Saturday and identified the body.
Ismail was the son of Jalal Uddin of Jamalpur Sadar upazila.
His son Hasan said Ismail had Tk 5 lakh and two mobile phones with him when he left Jamalpur. The money and phones were missing when his body was found.
Relatives said Ismail’s only daughter, Sharmin, was due to get married. He had sold land in his village to arrange the wedding and was returning to Gazipur to finalize the wedding date.
Hasan said his father left Jamalpur for Gazipur at around 3:30am on Thursday. He called Hasan at around 11pm and said he would arrive in the morning.
“He was returning to Gazipur to finalize the arrangements for my younger sister Sharmin’s wedding. He was supposed to set the wedding date after returning home,” Hasan said.
He said his father had sold 11% of land in the village for Tk 10.5 lakh for Sharmin’s wedding. He paid Tk 2 lakh to repay a loan and spent some of the money building a house in the village.
“He was returning to Gazipur with the remaining Tk 5 lakh in cash and some groceries. He also had an Android phone and a button phone. They were not found,” Hasan said.
Hasan said his father was supposed to get off at Jirani in Gazipur on Friday morning. He went there and called his father several times but found his phone switched off.
Later, Banani police informed Jamalpur police about the matter. Hasan then went to DMCH and identified his father’s body.
Nazrul Islam Talukdar, a sub-inspector of Banani police station, said Ismail’s identity was confirmed by matching his fingerprints with the National Identity Card database.
Citing relatives, Nazrul said Ismail had worked as a security guard at Delta Spinning Mill but left the job nine months ago due to illness. He lived with his wife, two children and daughter-in-law in Kashimpur, Gazipur.
Ismail had gone to his village home in Jamalpur about four months ago, where his mother and elder sister live.
“We suspect that he was strangled to death and the body was brought in a vehicle and dumped. We are collecting closed-circuit television camera footage to identify the vehicle. The victim’s family has filed a case,” Nazrul said.
Faridul Islam, officer-in-charge of Banani police station, told Dhaka Tribune that police had identified the vehicle used to dump Ismail’s body and flee the scene.
He said identifying the vehicle would help investigators determine who was involved in the incident.

item.title: IGP urges students to become honest, humane
item.description:
Inspector General of Police (IGP) Md Ali Hossain Fakir on Saturday urged students to build themselves as individuals with honesty, morality and human values.
“Merit helps a person move forward, but honesty, humanity and moral values make a person truly great,” he said while speaking as the chief guest at a scholarship distribution ceremony for children of police personnel who secured GPA-5 in the SSC, HSC and equivalent examinations in 2024 and 2025.
Police Headquarters organised the program at the Bangladesh Police Auditorium at Rajarbagh Police Lines in the capital. The scholarships were funded by the Bangladesh Police Welfare Trust.
The IGP said the recognition was not merely an award but a recognition of the students’ merit and hard work, the authorities’ confidence in their future and trust in their potential.
Fakir also warned them against drugs, saying they must remain alert against temporary curiosity or provocation that could lead them into addiction.
“Drugs are a deadly trap,” he said, adding that excessive addiction to mobile phones, social media and internet games could be as harmful as addiction to other intoxicating substances.
“Use technology, but remain alert so that technology cannot use you,” he said urging them to obey the law and encourage others to do the same.
Scholarship recipients Kazi Md Tanan Hossain, Syeda Sabiha Musharrat Mumu, Md Adnan Zawad and Mustaina Manzur shared their feelings at the event. Among the guardians, Additional DIG Shampa Yasmin and Police Inspector Sheikh Farukuzzaman also spoke.
A total of 801 students who secured GPA-5 in the 2024 SSC examinations and 272 in the HSC examinations received scholarships. In 2025, 845 SSC and 195 HSC GPA-5 achievers received the scholarships. 2,113 students received Bangladesh Police scholarships in the two years.
Of them, 360 Dhaka-based students were formally awarded scholarships at Saturday’s ceremony. The remaining scholarships will be distributed through the respective district police superintendent’s offices.

item.title: DMP files 3,206 cases for traffic violations
item.description:
The traffic division of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) on Saturday filed 3,206 cases against vehicles for violating traffic rules during the last two days in the capital.
The cases were filed as part of the DMP's regular enforcement campaign carried out on Thursday and Friday aimed at ensuring traffic discipline, reducing congestion and improving road safety across the city, according to a media and public relations division issued on Saturday.
The DMP said such drives against traffic law violators will continue, urging motorists and pedestrians alike to comply with traffic regulations to help maintain order on the roads.
It said that the DMP traffic police dumped 878 motor vehicles and towed 501 vehicles during the campaign. During the drives, the Traffic-Ramna Division filed 215 cases, including 19 against buses, 10 covered vans, 16 CNG-run auto-rickshaw and 71 motorcycles, according to a media spokesperson of the DMP.
The spokesperson said 228 cases were filed by the Traffic-Lalbagh Division including against 14 buses, 14 trucks, two covered vans, 13 CNG-run auto-rickshaws and 118 motorcycles, while Traffic-Motijheel Division filed 512 cases, against 29 buses, two trucks and 269 motorcycles.
Meanwhile, the Traffic-Wari Division filed 445 cases, including 50 against buses, 41 trucks, 31 covered vans, 50 CNG-run auto-rickshaws and 159 motorcycles.
The Traffic-Tejgaon Division filed 244 cases, including 13 against buses, one truck, eight covered vans, 24 CNG-run auto-rickshaws and 106 motorcycles.
The Traffic-Mirpur Division filed 669 cases, including 25 against buses, 22 trucks, 47 covered vans, 72 CNG-run auto-rickshaws and 258 motorcycles, Uttara division registered 612 cases including against 52 buses, 19 trucks, 23 covered vans, 54 CNG-run auto-rickshaws and 261 motorcycles.
The Traffic-Gulshan Division filed 273 cases, including 39 against buses, six trucks, eight covered vans, 29 CNG-run auto-rickshaws and 73 motorcycles.
The drives were conducted as part of the DMP's ongoing efforts to enforce traffic laws and ensure discipline on the city's roads, the DMP release said.

item.description:
The final of Miss World 2026 has concluded in Nha Trang, Vietnam, where Dominican Republic contestant Joheirry Mola won the crown as the best among contestants from 111 countries.

Joheirry Mola, who has been crowned Miss World previously won the Miss World Dominican Republic 2025 title. Her victory in that competition earned her the opportunity to represent her country on the global stage.

Joheirry Mola is a teacher, journalist, social worker and model. She runs an initiative called ‘Voice of Tomorrow’, which aims to teach English to disadvantaged children and young people and help them build confidence and develop skills needed for their future.

Spain’s Elisabeth Reynés was named first runner-up, while Malaysia’s Taanusiya Chetty was the second runner-up.

At the beginning of the final, the names of the top 40 contestants were announced. This was followed by the selection of the top 20, top 12 and top six.

The six finalists went through several rounds. The judges then asked them a range of questions before announcing the winner.

Miss World at 75

Miss World is the world’s oldest international beauty pageant. It was founded in the United Kingdom in 1951 by Eric Morley. Contestants are assessed through several stages, including various preliminary challenges, closed-door interviews and live events on stage.

This year’s Miss World pageant was held in Vietnam. For the first time, contestants from French Guiana, Eritrea, Mozambique, Pakistan and the Maldives took part.

Meanwhile, Ecuador’s Samantha Quenedit, Armenia’s Monika Harutjunjan and Togo’s Nadiratou Afolabi withdrew from the competition.

A total of 111 contestants took part in this year’s pageant. They were divided into four continental regions: Africa, the Americas and the Caribbean, Europe, and Asia and Oceania.

Bangladesh’s contestant Samanzar Sayeed had initially made it into the top six in her continental region in ‘Beauty with a Purpose’, but failed to secure a place in the top 40 at the final.

item.title: "Do not cover your face, you will be beaten," police to crying woman during video
item.description:
Detective Branch (DB) police are conducting a raid at a residential hotel in Dhaka. Several women have been detained during the operation.

The detained women are sitting in a room where they are being filmed. Those making the video repeatedly try to show the women’s faces. Yet, their faces could not be seen.

Some women try to cover their faces with the ends of their saris, while others use masks, scarves or their hands.

A video that has circulated online shows two female police officers holding the detained women and forcing them to show their faces. One woman can be seen crying. Nevertheless, they were told, "Remove everything, remove everything. Take off this mask. Do not cover up. If you cover up, you will be beaten."

The video was recorded on 12 August, when a DB team raided the New Rangdhanu Residential Hotel in the Abdullahpur bus stand area in Dhaka.

The video has been circulated by YouTubers as well as some news outlets.

The incident has raised questions over whether police can prevent a person from concealing their face if they do not want to be filmed. Human rights activists and lawyers say such conduct by police is unlawful and violates citizens’ rights.

Nur Khan, a former member of the National Human Rights Commission, told Prothom Alo that if a woman commits a crime, she should be tried and a court may punish her based on evidence. But the police are effectively arranging a form of punishment before trial. He termed this illegal.

Who ordered the women not to cover their faces?

Ilias Kabir, deputy commissioner (DC) of the DB’s Uttara division, was present during the raid at New Rangdhanu Residential Hotel.

Police sources said Ilias Kabir had ordered that the detained women not be allowed to cover their faces. In a video, he can be heard giving such an instruction while wearing a mask.

However, Ilias Kabir denied the allegation. On 2 September, he told Prothom Alo that detained people often wear masks to cover their faces and may be asked to remove them to confirm their identities.

“However, none of our members forced them to show their faces. The media people may have done that. They often do this for views and post the videos on Facebook,” he said.

When told that the video showed police officers forcing the women to remove the coverings from their faces, Ilias Kabir said, “Nothing was done intentionally. We try to do good work. There can be minor mistakes while doing so. We are human beings, not angels.”

One video after another

After watching the video of the raid at New Rangdhanu Residential Hotel, a series of similar videos kept appearing on this reporter's Facebook. Some show raids at hotels, while others were filmed during raids at bars or flats. YouTubers and some news outlets have circulated these videos.

Videos of men and women are also being recorded and circulated during routine searches at police checkpoints.

According to police and YouTuber sources, some police officers invite YouTubers to join raids beforehand. YouTubers and some news outlets then publish the footage to attract views, generating revenue from the content.

Raids at residential hotels and bars are not new. Such operations take place every year, yet so-called “antisocial” activities continue. There are allegations that some police officers receive monthly payments from hotels.

Saiful Alam Chowdhury, an Associate Professor of the Journalism Department at Dhaka University who previously worked as a journalist, told Prothom Alo that raids on residential hotels, bars and similar establishments are generally conducted when disputes arise over arrangements or financial transactions.

He compared taking YouTubers and some media personnel along during these raids to catching thieves with fanfare.

In Saiful Alam Chowdhury's view, YouTubers or journalists should not be taken along on any police raid. The police can hold a press conference after the raid. It is not appropriate to invite "content creators" alongside journalists to those press conferences.

He said some journalists are participating in unethical or illegal work for "views." He noted that the responsibility to control this lies with the respective news media.

What does the law say?

Article 35(5) of the Constitution of Bangladesh, under the protection in respect of trial and punishment, states that no person shall be subjected to torture or cruel, inhuman or degrading punishment or treatment.

Articles 2(1) and 4 of the United Nations Convention against Torture require member states to treat torture and cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment as offences and enact laws accordingly.

On 11 December 2012, the High Court directed that people arrested or detained as suspects should not be presented before the media.

The court also issued a rule asking why law enforcement agencies should not be directed to remain within the limits of their duties. The respondents, including the home secretary, inspector general of police, director general of the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) and commissioner of Dhaka Metropolitan Police, were asked to respond to the rule within two weeks.

Since the tenure of the previous interim government, the police, RAB, Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) and other forces have started blurring the faces of detained or arrested people in statements sent to the media.

The forces have adopted this practice, but the videos show that some officers are not following it. Instead, they are forcing detainees to show their faces.

Senior Advocate of the Supreme Court, Manzill Murshid, told Prothom Alo that the law does not permit this. Whatever the motive may be, illegal practices must be stopped.
